types.name: Arduino-class 8-bit AVR microcontroller board
types.description: A general-purpose development board built around an 8-bit AVR (ATmega328P, ATmega32U4, ATmega2560) running at 16 MHz from 5 V. It has a USB-serial bridge or native USB for the bootloader, a 5 V/3.3 V regulator and 0.1 in headers. Used in education, prototyping, hobby controllers and small fixtures.

sections.name: MCU and clock
sections.purpose: The ATmega target with its 16 MHz clock source and per-pin decoupling, plus the UCAP capacitor that USB AVRs (16U2/32U4) need.

parts.role: 16 MHz clock (resonator with built-in load caps)
Supply decoupling on VCC, AVCC and AREF (target and 16U2/32U4)
parts.qty: 1 per VCC/AVCC pin on each AVR plus 1 on AREF (4-8)

parts.role: UCAP internal USB regulator capacitor (ATmega16U2/32U4 only)

sections.name: Power entry and regulation
sections.purpose: Accept 7-12 V barrel input or USB 5 V, protect against reverse polarity and overcurrent, and generate 5 V and 3.3 V.

parts.role: Regulator input/output bulk capacitors (NCP1117 needs ≥10 µF on its output)

sections.name: USB-serial bridge
sections.purpose: USB device that exposes a serial port for the bootloader, with DTR-driven auto-reset (omitted on native-USB 32U4 boards).

parts.role: USB D+/D- series resistors (AVR USB requirement)

sections.name: Reset and programming
sections.purpose: Reset pull-up, auto-reset coupling from DTR, manual reset and ICSP access.

sections.name: Indicators and power auto-select
sections.purpose: Power, D13 user LED and TX/RX activity LEDs, plus the comparator and P-MOSFET that switch between USB and VIN power.

parts.role: D13 LED buffer / VIN-USB auto-select comparator

checks: Every VCC and AVCC pin has a 100 nF capacitor placed directly at the pin, and AREF has its own 100 nF to GND
The 16 MHz crystal or resonator sits within a few mm of XTAL1/XTAL2, with load caps (if a bare crystal) returning to a short GND path
RESET has a 10 kΩ pull-up, a 100 nF DTR coupling capacitor and a clamp diode to VCC so auto-reset pulses stay within the pin's limits
The 5 V regulator's input sits behind a reverse-polarity diode, its output has at least 10 µF, and the USB VBUS path has a 500 mA PTC fuse
The board switches cleanly between USB and VIN power (comparator plus P-MOSFET, or diode-OR), so VIN never back-feeds the USB host
An ATmega16U2 or 32U4 has 22 Ω series resistors on D+/D-, a 1 µF capacitor on UCAP, and an ESD array next to the USB connector
Each LED has its own series resistor sized for 2-10 mA
The ICSP header pinout matches the standard AVR 2x3 (MISO, VCC, SCK, MOSI, RESET, GND)

types.name: ESP32 / Wi-Fi IoT board
types.description: A board built around an Espressif ESP32, ESP32-S3/C3 or ESP8266 module with an on-module antenna. It has a 3.3 V regulator sized for Wi-Fi transmit peaks, USB (through a bridge or native) with DTR/RTS auto-program, and BOOT/EN buttons. Used for IoT sensors, smart-home devices, data loggers and connected controllers.

sections.name: Wireless module and decoupling
sections.purpose: Pre-certified module (crystal, flash and RF match inside) with the supply capacitance Espressif's hardware design guidelines specify.

parts.role: 3V3 decoupling at module supply pin and at each bridge-IC supply pin
parts.qty: 1-2 at module plus 1 per bridge supply pin

parts.role: 3V3 bulk capacitor at module (Wi-Fi TX bursts)

sections.name: Power supply
sections.purpose: Convert USB 5 V (or battery) to 3.3 V with at least 500 mA capability for Wi-Fi transmit peaks.

parts.role: VBUS OR-ing / reverse-protection Schottky (rated above the Wi-Fi peak current)

sections.name: USB, bridge and auto-program
sections.purpose: USB-C sink connector, a USB-UART bridge for the classic ESP32, and a two-transistor DTR/RTS circuit that drives EN and GPIO0.

parts.role: USB-to-UART bridge (not needed on S3/C3 native USB)

sections.name: Reset, boot and strapping
sections.purpose: EN RC delay so the chip resets only after 3V3 is stable, a GPIO0 boot button, and safe default levels on the strapping pins.

sections.name: Battery charging (optional)
sections.purpose: Single-cell Li-ion/LiPo charging for portable nodes (Feather-style boards), with input/output capacitors and a charge-status LED.

parts.role: Li-ion linear charger (no thermistor input; use MCP73833 or BQ24074 if NTC monitoring is required)

checks: The module antenna overhangs the board edge or has a copper-free keep-out on every layer under and around it, as the module datasheet specifies
The 3.3 V regulator is rated for at least 500 mA, with 10-22 µF bulk plus 100 nF placed at the module 3V3 pin
EN has a 10 kΩ pull-up and 1 µF to GND, so the chip comes out of reset only after the supply has settled
Strapping pins (GPIO0, GPIO2, GPIO5, GPIO12/MTDI, GPIO15 on ESP32) are not loaded by peripherals in a way that forces a wrong boot mode or a wrong flash voltage
The DTR/RTS auto-program circuit uses two cross-coupled NPN transistors, so both lines asserted together never hold the chip in reset
USB-C has separate 5.1 kΩ pull-downs on CC1 and CC2 (not one shared resistor) and an ESD array next to the connector
No ground pour, traces or metal parts sit in the antenna keep-out, and the module ground pad has stitching vias
A Li-ion charger has 4.7 µF on its input and output, and either the cell has its own protection/NTC or the charger has a thermistor (TS/THERM) input

types.name: STM32 / Cortex-M development board
types.description: A 32-bit Arm Cortex-M board (STM32, GD32, SAM D/E, nRF52, LPC) with a 3.3 V regulator, HSE/LSE crystals, filtered analog supply, SWD debug header, BOOT0 strap and USB full-speed. Used for embedded firmware development, motor and industrial controllers, and as the core of many products.

sections.name: MCU supply decoupling
sections.purpose: Decoupling as given in the STM32 hardware-development application notes (AN2586 for F1, AN4488 for F4): 100 nF per VDD, 4.7 µF bulk, VCAP where present, and a filtered VDDA.

parts.role: VDD bulk / VCAP (F411 single VCAP_1 needs 4.7 µF low-ESR; F405/F407 use 2×2.2 µF; check datasheet)

sections.name: Clocks
sections.purpose: HSE crystal for an accurate PLL and USB clock, and an LSE crystal for the RTC.

parts.value: 8 MHz (or 25 MHz on F411 Black Pill), 18 pF CL

parts.role: LSE 32.768 kHz RTC crystal (verify gain margin per AN2867; low-drive LSE prefers 6-7 pF CL parts)

parts.value: ≈18 pF C0G for 12.5 pF CL (2×(CL−~3 pF stray))

sections.name: Reset, boot and debug
sections.purpose: NRST filtering, BOOT0 strap, and an SWD header for an ST-Link/J-Link.

sections.name: USB full-speed device
sections.purpose: USB-C sink connector with ESD protection; STM32F1 (F102/F103) parts also need an external 1.5 kΩ D+ pull-up.

parts.role: D+ pull-up to 3.3 V (STM32F1 only; F0/F4/L4/G4 have an internal pull-up)

sections.name: Power and indicators
sections.purpose: 5 V to 3.3 V regulation, input protection, and power/user LEDs.

parts.role: Regulator input/output bulk capacitors (LD1117 needs ≥10 µF on its output)

checks: Every VDD pin has a 100 nF capacitor within about 2 mm, and the 4.7 µF bulk capacitor sits near the MCU
VDDA/VREF+ is filtered (ferrite plus 1 µF and 10 nF) and is never left unconnected, even when the ADC is unused
VCAP pin(s) on STM32F4/F7/H7 have the low-ESR capacitor value given in the datasheet, and no ordinary decoupling cap is fitted in its place
BOOT0 is pulled down with 10 kΩ (or set by the option byte), so the part boots from flash
The HSE and LSE crystals sit next to the OSC pins, with load caps sized from CL as 2×(CL−Cstray) and no traces routed under the crystal
The SWD header carries SWDIO, SWCLK, NRST, GND and VTref in the standard Cortex 10-pin order
On STM32F1 a 1.5 kΩ D+ pull-up is present (not 10 kΩ as on some clones); USB-C has separate 5.1 kΩ CC pull-downs

types.name: FPGA development board
types.description: A board built around an FPGA (Xilinx/AMD 7-series, Lattice iCE40/ECP5, Intel MAX 10/Cyclone, Gowin) with a multi-rail power tree, an SPI configuration flash, an oscillator, and a USB-JTAG bridge (usually an FTDI FT2232H). Used for digital-logic teaching, hardware prototyping, signal processing and soft-core CPUs.

sections.name: FPGA and configuration
sections.purpose: The FPGA, its SPI configuration flash and the configuration-control pull-ups.

parts.role: PROGRAM_B / INIT_B / CS pull-ups (DONE often 330 Ω per UG470)
DONE LED series resistor / DONE pull-up

sections.name: Power tree
sections.purpose: Generate the core (≈1.0-1.2 V), auxiliary (1.8 V) and I/O (3.3 V) rails in the order the FPGA family requires.

parts.role: Feedback divider resistors (set each rail voltage)

sections.name: FPGA decoupling
sections.purpose: High-frequency and mid-frequency decoupling on every supply bank, per the vendor's PCB design guide (e.g. Xilinx UG483).

sections.name: Clock
sections.purpose: Single-ended CMOS oscillator feeding a clock-capable FPGA pin.

sections.name: USB-JTAG and UART bridge
sections.purpose: Dual-channel FTDI bridge: channel A for JTAG configuration, channel B for UART.

parts.role: Crystal load capacitors (FT2232H datasheet uses 27 pF)

sections.name: USB input and protection
sections.purpose: USB connector that powers the board and carries JTAG/UART, with ESD protection and VBUS current limiting.

checks: Rails power up in the sequence the FPGA datasheet requires (for 7-series: VCCINT, then VCCBRAM, VCCAUX, then VCCO), using regulator enable/PG chaining
Every VCCINT, VCCAUX and VCCO bank has the per-ball 100 nF count from the vendor PCB guide, placed on the back side under the BGA
Configuration-mode pins (M[2:0] or equivalent) are strapped for SPI master boot, and PROGRAM_B, INIT_B and DONE have their pull-ups
The configuration flash part and density are on the vendor's supported list, and it is wired to the dedicated CCLK/CS/D0-D3 pins
The oscillator feeds a clock-capable (MRCC/SRCC/GBIN) pin and runs from the VCCO voltage of its bank
JTAG TCK/TMS/TDI/TDO run from the FT2232H channel A with matching VCCIO, the FT2232H has its 12 kΩ REF resistor, and a JTAG header is broken out for an external probe
Unused banks still have VCCO tied to a valid rail, as the datasheet requires
BGA FPGAs use at least four layers with solid ground and power planes under the BGA (small QFN iCE40 boards can be 2-layer)

types.name: Raspberry Pi HAT / Arduino shield (add-on board)
types.description: An add-on board that plugs onto a host's header (Raspberry Pi 40-pin GPIO or Arduino Uno R3 shield layout) to add peripherals such as motor drivers, sensors, displays, relays or ADCs. It draws power from the host, so it must respect the host's logic levels and current limits. A Pi HAT must also follow the ID EEPROM and back-powering rules.

sections.name: Host connector
sections.purpose: Mechanical and electrical connection to the host board, at the correct pitch and position.

sections.name: HAT ID EEPROM (Pi HAT only)
sections.purpose: I2C EEPROM on ID_SD/ID_SC (GPIO0/1) that holds the HAT descriptor and device-tree overlay, as the HAT specification requires.

parts.role: ID EEPROM at address 0x50 (A0-A2 to GND)

sections.name: Power and back-power protection
sections.purpose: Local regulation and an ideal-diode or Schottky path, so a HAT that feeds 5 V cannot back-drive the host or the host's USB supply.

parts.role: Local 3.3 V regulator (avoid loading the host's 3V3)

sections.name: Logic-level interface
sections.purpose: Translate between 3.3 V Pi GPIO (not 5 V tolerant) or 5 V Arduino I/O and the add-on's peripherals.

parts.role: Bidirectional level translator (light loads only; auto-direction)
I2C pull-ups (Arduino shields only; the Pi already has 1.8 kΩ on GPIO2/3)

checks: Board outline, mounting holes and header position match the HAT mechanical spec (65x56.5 mm, 4x M2.5 holes) or the Arduino Uno R3 shield outline, including the offset header
A Pi HAT has the ID EEPROM on GPIO0/GPIO1 (ID_SD/ID_SC) at address 0x50, with WP pulled up to protect the descriptor
No 5 V signal reaches a Raspberry Pi GPIO; 3.3 V/5 V translation is present wherever the add-on's peripherals run at 5 V
If the add-on supplies 5 V to the host, an ideal diode or Schottky prevents back-feeding and a PTC limits current
No extra I2C pull-ups on Pi GPIO2/3, which already have 1.8 kΩ on the Pi; an Arduino shield adds 4.7 kΩ only if no other device on the bus provides them
The total current drawn from the host's 3.3 V and 5 V pins stays within the host's budget (Pi 3V3 rail headroom is small; use a local regulator)
Tall components and connectors clear the host's USB/Ethernet jacks, and stacking headers are used if further boards must stack on top

types.name: Sensor breakout board
types.description: A small board that carries a single sensor IC (environmental, IMU, light, distance, current or ADC) with its decoupling, an optional regulator and level shifting, I2C/SPI pull-ups, and 0.1 in or Qwiic/STEMMA QT connectors. Used to prototype and connect sensors to microcontroller boards.

sections.name: Sensor IC
sections.purpose: The sensing device with decoupling as specified in its datasheet.

sections.name: Power and level shifting
sections.purpose: Let a 3.3 V sensor run from 3-5 V hosts: an LDO for VIN, plus MOSFET level shifters on the open-drain I2C lines.

sections.name: Bus interface
sections.purpose: I2C pull-ups (on solder-jumper pads so they can be disconnected), address select, and a CS strap to choose I2C or SPI mode.

parts.role: CS pull-up (selects I2C on dual-mode sensors)

sections.name: Connectors and indicator
sections.purpose: Daisy-chain Qwiic/STEMMA QT ports, a 0.1 in header and a power LED.

checks: The sensor supply pins have the decoupling the datasheet specifies, placed right at the pins
I2C pull-ups go through cuttable solder jumpers, so a bus with several breakouts does not end up with too low a combined pull-up
The Qwiic/STEMMA QT pinout is GND, 3V3, SDA, SCL, and only 3.3 V reaches that connector
Dual-mode sensors have CS tied high for I2C, and the address pin is strapped rather than left floating
If the board accepts 5 V, both the supply (LDO) and the logic (BSS138 or translator) are shifted, so the sensor never sees 5 V
Heat-sensitive sensors (humidity, temperature, pressure) sit away from the regulator and LED, with slots or keep-outs that limit thermal coupling
The board outline has mounting holes, and the silkscreen labels every pin and the I2C address

types.name: Debug probe / programmer (ST-Link, J-Link class)
types.description: A USB-connected in-circuit debugger and flash programmer. An on-board MCU runs ST-Link, CMSIS-DAP or J-Link firmware and drives SWD/JTAG to a target through level translators powered from the target's VTref. Often includes a virtual COM port and switchable target power. Used on development benches and production programming stations.

sections.name: Probe MCU
sections.purpose: Runs the debug firmware and the USB device stack.

parts.qty: 1 per VDD pin plus 1 on NRST

sections.name: Target interface
sections.purpose: Translate SWD/JTAG/UART signals to the target's VTref voltage (1.65-5.5 V), with series damping and ESD protection on the cable side.

parts.role: Series damping resistors on target lines

sections.name: Probe power and target supply
sections.purpose: 3.3 V supply for the probe from USB, plus an optional current-limited, firmware-switchable supply to the target.

sections.name: USB and indicators
sections.purpose: Host connection with ESD protection, and status LEDs for communication and target state.

checks: Target-side translators take VCCB from the target's VTref pin, not from the probe's 3.3 V, so the probe drives at the target's logic level
With no target attached (VTref = 0 V), the translators are in their isolated state and the probe drives no target pins
SWDIO, SWCLK, NRST and SWO have 22-47 Ω series resistors and an ESD array next to the target connector
The Cortex 10-pin connector pin 1 and the keying match the Arm standard; pin 1 is marked on the silkscreen
Any target power output passes through a current-limited load switch or PTC and is off by default
The USB interface has ESD protection, CC pull-downs on USB-C, and a D+ pull-up if the probe MCU lacks one
NRST is driven open-drain (or through the translator with a pull-up on the target side), so it never fights the target's reset circuit

types.name: USB-to-UART adapter
types.description: A small dongle that turns USB into a TTL serial port using a bridge IC (FTDI FT232R/FT231X, Silicon Labs CP2102N, WCH CH340, Prolific PL2303). It usually has a 3.3 V/5 V I/O selector, TX/RX LEDs and a 6-pin FTDI-style header carrying DTR for auto-reset. Used to flash and debug microcontrollers and to read serial consoles on embedded Linux boards.

sections.name: USB-UART bridge
sections.purpose: The bridge IC with the supply and regulator capacitors its datasheet requires.

parts.role: Alternative low-cost bridge (internal oscillator, no crystal)

sections.name: USB input
sections.purpose: Connector, ESD, VBUS filtering and overcurrent protection.

sections.name: I/O voltage select
sections.purpose: Sets the UART logic level (3.3 V or 5 V) and the VCC supplied on the header.

parts.role: 3.3 V regulator (when the bridge's internal 3V3 cannot supply the target)

sections.name: Serial header and indicators
sections.purpose: 6-pin FTDI-style output with series protection, plus TX/RX activity LEDs.

parts.role: 6-pin header (GND, CTS, VCC, TXD, RXD, DTR)
DTR auto-reset coupling capacitor (for Arduino targets)

checks: VIO on the bridge (VCCIO on FT232R, VIO on CP2102N) follows the selected logic level, so TXD/RTS/DTR swing to 3.3 V or 5 V as labelled
The header pinout matches the FTDI 6-pin convention (GND, CTS, VCC, TXD, RXD, DTR/RTS) and the silkscreen states the I/O voltage
A CH340G has its 12 MHz crystal with 22 pF load caps; a CH340C/CH340E and the CP2102N need no crystal
USB-C has separate 5.1 kΩ CC pull-downs and an ESD array next to the connector
The VCC pin on the header is fused (PTC) so a short at the target cannot pull the USB host's VBUS down
TX/RX LEDs are driven from the bridge's dedicated activity outputs (CBUS/GPIO), not loaded onto the UART lines themselves
The bridge's 3V3 output is not asked to source more than the datasheet limit (≈50-100 mA); an external LDO is fitted if the header powers the target at 3.3 V

types.name: RP2040 microcontroller board
types.description: A board built on the Raspberry Pi RP2040 (or RP2350) dual-core MCU. The chip has no internal flash, so it needs an external QSPI flash, a 12 MHz crystal, the core-regulator capacitors, a BOOTSEL button, and USB with 27 Ω series resistors. Used for hobby and education boards, keyboards, USB gadgets and low-cost products.

sections.name: MCU and QSPI flash
sections.purpose: The RP2040 with its boot flash on the dedicated QSPI pins and a BOOTSEL button that forces USB boot mode.

sections.name: Supply decoupling and core regulator
sections.purpose: IOVDD/ADC decoupling, the 1 µF capacitors the internal 1.1 V core LDO needs, and bulk capacitance for the 3.3 V regulator.

parts.role: 3.3 V regulator input/output and 3V3 bulk capacitors

sections.name: Crystal oscillator
sections.purpose: 12 MHz reference for the PLLs and USB, in the configuration given in the RP2040 hardware design guide.

sections.name: USB and power input
sections.purpose: USB-C device port with the required 27 Ω series resistors, VBUS protection and a 3.3 V regulator.

parts.role: USB D+/D- series resistors (required by RP2040)

sections.name: Debug and indicator
sections.purpose: SWD access for the Raspberry Pi Debug Probe, plus a user LED.

checks: USB_DP and USB_DM each have a 27 Ω series resistor placed close to the RP2040, and are routed as a 90 Ω differential pair
VREG_VIN and VREG_VOUT each have a 1 µF capacitor, and VREG_VOUT is tied to both DVDD pins, each with 100 nF
Every IOVDD, USB_VDD and ADC_AVDD pin has its own 100 nF capacitor right at the pin
The 12 MHz crystal has its load caps (about 15 pF for a 10 pF CL part) and the 1 kΩ series resistor on XOUT, all within a few mm of XIN/XOUT
QSPI flash lines are short and direct, and BOOTSEL pulls QSPI_SS to GND through 1 kΩ
The flash part supports 03h serial read and the quad-read mode the second-stage bootloader (boot2) expects (W25Q-series or equivalent)
VBUS feeds VSYS through a Schottky (or ideal diode), so USB and battery/VSYS sources can coexist without back-feeding, and the 3.3 V regulator has its input/output capacitors
USB-C has separate 5.1 kΩ CC pull-downs and an ESD array at the connector

types.name: PC motherboard (ATX / micro-ATX)
types.description: Main board of a desktop PC. It carries the CPU socket and its multiphase VRM, the DIMM slots, the chipset (PCH), PCIe x16/x1 slots, M.2 sockets, SATA ports, rear I/O (USB, LAN, audio) and the ATX/EPS power connectors. It comes as ATX (305 x 244 mm), micro-ATX (244 x 244 mm) or mini-ITX (170 x 170 mm) for consumer, workstation and industrial PCs.

sections.name: CPU core VRM
sections.purpose: Multiphase buck that converts 12 V EPS to Vcore with load-line regulation and fast transient response

parts.role: Output MLCC array in and under the socket

sections.name: Memory and platform rails
sections.purpose: DDR termination and local decoupling for the PCH, Super I/O and audio supplies

parts.qty: 1 (DDR4 boards; DDR5 DIMMs have their own PMIC)

sections.name: Firmware, RTC and Super I/O
sections.purpose: BIOS storage, real-time clock with coin-cell backup, and hardware monitoring and fan control

parts.role: Super I/O / hardware monitor / fan controller

sections.name: Networking and audio
sections.purpose: Wired LAN controller with its reference clock, and the HD-audio codec

parts.value: 22-27 pF C0G 50 V for a CL 18 pF crystal (= 2 x (CL - Cstray))

sections.name: I/O protection, fans and power entry
sections.purpose: ESD and overcurrent protection on external ports, fan headers, and the main power connectors

checks: Every PCH, Super I/O, LAN and codec supply pin has a 100 nF X7R capacitor within about 2 mm, with a short via to the ground plane
Vcore phase count, power-stage rating and output capacitance (polymer plus MLCC) meet the CPU vendor's VRM spec for Iccmax, load line and transients
The EPS 8-pin (plus optional 4/8-pin) and ATX 24-pin headers have enough contacts for the CPU current (about 7-8 A per Mini-Fit Jr pin) and sit next to the VRM input
The RTC has a CR2032 holder OR-ed through a Schottky (BAT54C) with standby power, and the 32.768 kHz crystal and its two load capacitors are next to the PCH RTC pins
Every external USB port has ESD protection at the connector and a current-limited VBUS (power switch or PTC)
PCIe pairs are routed at 85 Ω differential and USB at 90 Ω with intra-pair length matching, and AC-coupling capacitors are on the TX side only
BIOS flash can be reprogrammed for recovery (dual BIOS, flashback or programming header)
DDR4 boards have a VTT regulator with 10 µF and 100 nF decoupling at the end of the fly-by bus; DDR5 boards deliver 5 V (UDIMM) bulk power to the DIMM PMIC

types.name: Single-board computer (Raspberry Pi class)
types.description: A board between credit-card size and 100 mm that combines an Arm application SoC, LPDDR RAM, boot storage (microSD or eMMC), power regulation, Ethernet, USB, HDMI and a 40-pin GPIO header. It is used for education, hobby projects, kiosks, IoT gateways and embedded Linux products.

sections.name: Power input
sections.purpose: USB-C 5 V sink input with protection and the main step-down rails

parts.role: Synchronous buck for 3.3 V / 1.8 V / core rails

sections.name: SoC and LPDDR memory
sections.purpose: Decoupling, reference clock and DRAM calibration around the application processor

parts.value: 24 MHz, CL 18 pF (Rockchip/Allwinner/Amlogic); BCM2711 uses 54 MHz
22-27 pF C0G for a CL 18 pF crystal (= 2 x (CL - Cstray))
240 Ω 1% (to VDDQ on LPDDR4/4X; to VSS on DDR3/DDR4)

sections.name: Gigabit Ethernet
sections.purpose: External PHY (where not on-SoC), clock and RJ45 with magnetics

parts.value: 22-27 pF C0G for a CL 18 pF crystal

parts.role: RJ45 with integrated magnetics and LEDs

sections.name: USB, HDMI and storage I/O
sections.purpose: Protected external ports and the boot media socket

sections.name: GPIO header and status
sections.purpose: Raspberry Pi-compatible expansion header and indicator LEDs

checks: The USB-C input has a separate 5.1 kΩ pull-down on each CC pin (not one shared resistor), so standard chargers supply 5 V
The input path is rated for full load (3 A Pi 4 class, 5 A Pi 5 class) and has a TVS and reverse/overcurrent protection
Every SoC and LPDDR supply group has 100 nF close to the balls plus bulk, and PMIC/buck sequencing follows the SoC datasheet
LPDDR byte lanes are length-matched, and each ZQ pin has a 240 Ω 1% resistor to the rail the DRAM datasheet names (VDDQ for LPDDR4/4X)
Crystal load capacitors are calculated from the crystal CL and placed next to the SoC/PHY pins with a guard ground
Every user-facing connector (USB, HDMI, Ethernet, SD) has ESD protection at the connector
The 40-pin header follows the Raspberry Pi pinout (5 V on pins 2/4, 3.3 V logic, ID_SD/ID_SC on 27/28)
The SoC has thermal copper and a heatsink or fan provision

types.name: Compute-module carrier board
types.description: Carrier (base or IO) board for a system-on-module such as the Raspberry Pi CM4/CM5, NVIDIA Jetson, or SMARC/Qseven modules. The module holds the SoC, RAM, eMMC and PMIC. The carrier provides the input power, the high-density mating connectors and the application I/O: Ethernet magnetics, USB, HDMI, PCIe/M.2, GPIO, RTC and fan control.
examples: Raspberry Pi Compute Module 4 IO Board
Raspberry Pi Compute Module 5 IO Board
NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Developer Kit carrier (P3768)

sections.name: Module interface
sections.purpose: High-density mating connectors and local decoupling at the module power pins

sections.name: Power input
sections.purpose: 12 V (or USB-C 5 V) input, protection and 5 V regulation for the module and peripherals

parts.role: 12 V to 5 V synchronous buck (≥ 5 A for CM5 / peripherals)

sections.name: Ethernet and USB
sections.purpose: Magnetics for the module's on-board PHY, plus a USB hub and protected ports

parts.role: RJ45 with integrated magnetics and LEDs

parts.value: 22-27 pF C0G for a CL 18 pF crystal

sections.name: Display, PCIe and peripherals
sections.purpose: HDMI, PCIe/M.2 expansion, RTC and fan control

parts.role: I2C real-time clock (internal selectable load caps)

parts.value: 32.768 kHz, CL 12.5 pF (set PCF85063 CAP_SEL to 12.5 pF)

sections.name: Status and control
sections.purpose: GPIO header, boot-mode button, indicator LEDs and I2C pull-ups

checks: The board-to-board connector footprint, orientation, pin 1 and stack height match the module datasheet, and module mounting holes line up
The carrier supplies the module input within tolerance (for example 5 V ±5% at ≥ 3 A for CM4, ≥ 5 A for CM5), with bulk capacitors at the connector
The input path has a fuse or eFuse, a TVS and reverse-polarity protection rated for the full input voltage
PCIe (85 Ω), USB (90 Ω), HDMI and Ethernet MDI (100 Ω) pairs are impedance-controlled and length-matched over an unbroken reference plane
Ethernet magnetics sit on the carrier, wired to the module's MDI pins and centre-tap guidance
Every external connector has ESD protection and every USB port has a current-limited VBUS
The RTC crystal CL matches the PCF85063 internal capacitor setting, and a backup battery or supercap is provided if timekeeping must survive power loss
The boot/flash control pins (nRPIBOOT, EEPROM_nWP, GLOBAL_EN or the Jetson recovery pin) are reachable by switch or jumper

types.name: Graphics card (discrete GPU)

It also has display outputs (DisplayPort, HDMI) and fan and LED control. It is used in gaming PCs, workstations and AI/compute servers.

types.description: Dense 8-12 layer notebook board. It also holds the BIOS SPI flash, M.2 SSD and Wi-Fi sockets, the eDP display link and many FPC connectors to daughterboards.
examples: Lenovo ThinkPad T14 Gen 4 system board

types.name: Smartphone mainboard
types.description: Highly integrated any-layer HDI board, often stacked as a sandwich. Most passives are 0201 or 01005, under RF shield cans.
examples: Samsung Galaxy S23 mainboard (Snapdragon 8 Gen 2, SM8550)

types.name: Server backplane / PCIe riser
types.description: Interconnect boards inside servers, passive or lightly active. PCIe risers move x8/x16 slots from the motherboard into another orientation. Drive backplanes connect NVMe (U.2/E3.S) or SAS/SATA drives to the host with hot-plug power, presence detection and status LEDs. Higher PCIe generations add redrivers or retimers and clock buffers, and management runs over I2C/SMBus.
examples: HPE ProLiant DL380 Gen10 NVMe drive backplane
Intel Server System M50CYP 2U NVMe backplane
Open Compute Project Yosemite V3 riser

types.name: SSD (NVMe M.2) board
types.description: M.2 card (2230/2242/2280) carrying an NVMe controller, NAND flash packages, an optional DRAM cache, and point-of-load regulators fed from the single M.2 3.3 V rail. It connects to the host over PCIe x4 through an M-key edge connector and is used in desktops, laptops, consoles and servers.

types.name: Memory module (DDR4 / DDR5 DIMM and SO-DIMM)
types.description: JEDEC-standard module carrying 4-18 DRAM devices (36 on large RDIMMs) on a fly-by command/address bus, plus an SPD EEPROM (an SPD hub with temperature sensor on DDR5). DDR5 modules add an on-module PMIC, and registered modules add an RCD. Used in desktops (UDIMM, 133.35 mm), laptops (SO-DIMM, 69.6 mm) and servers (RDIMM/LRDIMM).
examples: JEDEC DDR4 UDIMM raw card A

sections.purpose: Memory devices with per-device calibration and supply decoupling

sections.name: SPD and thermal sensing

sections.name: DDR5 on-module PMIC rails
sections.purpose: Passives around the JEDEC PMIC (PMIC5000/5010/5100 class) that generates VDD, VDDQ and VPP from 5 V (client) or 12 V (server) input

Each DRAM has its own 240 Ω 1% ZQ resistor and 2-4 x 100 nF on VDD/VDDQ placed next to the balls
CA/CTL/CLK follow fly-by topology and are terminated to VTT at the end of the chain, with VTT decoupled
SPD is programmed with valid JEDEC data (plus XMP/EXPO profiles if sold), with SA0-SA2 wired to the edge pins as specified

types.name: AC-DC flyback switch-mode power supply
types.description: Converts universal mains (90-264 VAC) into an isolated low-voltage DC output (typically 5-24 V, 5-65 W). It uses a bridge rectifier, a high-voltage bulk capacitor, a primary-side switcher or controller driving a flyback transformer, and optocoupler/TL431 feedback across the isolation barrier. Used in phone chargers, wall adapters, appliance auxiliary supplies and open-frame PSUs.
examples: Mean Well IRM-10 / IRM-20 encapsulated AC-DC modules
TI UCC28740 5 V / 10 W USB charger reference designs
Generic 5 V 2 A USB wall adapters

sections.name: Mains input and protection
sections.purpose: Fuse the line, clamp surges, limit inrush and suppress differential-mode EMI before rectification.

parts.role: Input fuse, time-lag, first component on the line conductor

sections.name: Rectifier and HV bulk
sections.purpose: Full-wave rectify the mains and store energy on the ~340 V DC bus.

parts.value: 10-47 µF 400 V 105 °C (about 2-3 µF per watt at universal input)

sections.name: Primary switching and snubber
sections.purpose: Switch the transformer primary and clamp leakage-inductance spikes on the drain.

parts.role: Integrated off-line switcher (controller + 725 V MOSFET) or flyback controller

parts.value: 100 kΩ (split across several 1206 for voltage and dissipation)

sections.purpose: Transfer energy across the isolation barrier and regulate the output through an optocoupler.

parts.role: Flyback transformer (custom wound to the design)
parts.value: Primary inductance and turns ratio per design, reinforced insulation

parts.role: Shunt reference for the secondary error amplifier

sections.purpose: Rectify and filter the secondary winding into a low-ripple DC output.

parts.value: 60 V 5 A Schottky (Vr above Vout + Vin_max/N)

checks: The fuse is the first part on the line conductor, and every primary part is rated for 264 VAC plus surge (bulk capacitor at least 400 V, clamp diode and switch at least 650-700 V).

Creepage and clearance between primary and secondary meet reinforced insulation (typically at least 6.4 mm creepage, with a routed slot under the transformer and optocoupler where needed), and no copper or vias cross the barrier.
Only safety-rated X2 capacitors go across L-N and only Y1/Y2 capacitors bridge primary to secondary; a bleeder resistor discharges the X-capacitor when it exceeds about 0.1 µF.
The primary switching loop (bulk capacitor to transformer primary to switch to bulk return) and the secondary loop (winding to rectifier to output capacitor) are kept as small as possible.
The RCD clamp is rated for the leakage spike and keeps the drain under the switch's BVDSS with margin at high line.
The output capacitor's ripple-current rating covers the secondary RMS current, and the voltage rating is at least 1.5 times Vout.
The TL431 has enough cathode bias current (at least 1 mA through the optocoupler LED plus its bias resistor) and the loop has compensation components.
Hot parts (switcher, rectifier, transformer) have copper heat-spreading and are kept away from the electrolytic capacitors.

types.name: DC-DC buck converter module
types.description: A non-isolated step-down converter that turns a higher DC input (typically 7-40 V) into a regulated lower rail (1.2-12 V) at 0.5-5 A with 85-95 % efficiency. It is built around a buck regulator IC, a power inductor, a catch diode (asynchronous) or internal synchronous FET, and input and output ceramic capacitors. It is sold as a standalone module and also used as the main rail generator on most embedded boards.
examples: Diodes AP63203 3.3 V buck reference design

sections.purpose: Supply the pulsed input current locally and protect the IC from transients and reverse polarity.

parts.role: Input ceramic capacitor, right at VIN/GND pins
Input bulk electrolytic (long or inductive input leads)
Input TVS (standoff at or above max Vin, clamp below IC abs max)
parts.value: e.g. 24 V standoff 600 W for inputs up to 24 V

sections.name: Switching stage
sections.purpose: Regulator IC, energy-storage inductor and freewheel path.

parts.value: 10 µH, Isat at least 1.3 x peak current

sections.name: Feedback and compensation
sections.purpose: Set the output voltage and stabilise the control loop.

sections.name: Output and indication
sections.purpose: Filter output ripple, show power-good and bring the rail out.

parts.value: 22 µF 25 V X5R (allow for DC-bias derating)

checks: The input ceramic capacitor sits within about 2 mm of VIN and PGND, so the hot loop (Cin to high-side switch to diode or low-side FET to Cin) is minimal.
The SW node copper is only as large as the current needs, and the feedback trace runs away from the SW node and the inductor, with the divider placed next to the FB pin.
Inductor saturation current is at least 1.2-1.3 times the peak switch current and the value matches the datasheet ripple target (about 30 % of Iout).
Ceramic output capacitance is checked after DC-bias derating (a 22 µF 25 V 1206 may give only 10-12 µF at 12 V).
The catch diode (if used) is rated at least Vin_max reverse and handles Iout x (1 - D) average.
The TVS standoff is at or above the maximum operating input and its clamping voltage is below the regulator's absolute-maximum VIN; if no standard TVS fits, the input range is derated instead.
Any exposed thermal pad has a via array to an internal or bottom ground plane.
Vout = Vref x (1 + Rtop/Rbottom) is recalculated from the actual 1 % resistor values.

types.name: Boost converter module
types.description: A non-isolated step-up converter that raises a low input (a single Li-ion cell, 2xAA, or 5 V USB) to a higher rail such as 5 V, 12 V or 24 V. It consists of a boost IC (internal switch, optionally synchronous), a power inductor, a Schottky rectifier for asynchronous parts, and input and output capacitors. Used in battery-powered devices, USB-to-12 V adapters and LED backlight rails.
examples: Microchip MCP1640 single-cell boost reference designs

sections.purpose: Decouple the input and carry the full inductor current from the source.

parts.role: Input ceramic capacitor near the inductor and IC GND
Input HF bypass at VIN pin

sections.purpose: Store energy in the inductor and switch it to the output.

parts.value: 1 µH for TPS61023 (1-22 µH per the chosen IC's datasheet), Isat at least peak input current

parts.role: Rectifier Schottky (asynchronous boost such as MT3608 or XL6009 only)
parts.value: 40 V 3 A Schottky, Vr above Vout

sections.name: Output and feedback
sections.purpose: Filter the pulsed output current and set the output voltage.

parts.role: Output ceramic capacitors (close to the diode or IC VOUT and GND)
parts.value: 22 µF 25 V X5R (for outputs up to about 12 V; use higher-voltage parts for 24 V)

sections.name: Protection and indication
sections.purpose: Limit fault current (a boost cannot interrupt a shorted output) and show status.

parts.role: Resettable PTC on input or output

checks: The output capacitor and rectifier, or the IC VOUT pin, form the tight hot loop in a boost: the output capacitor sits within about 2 mm of the diode cathode or VOUT and the IC ground.
Inductor saturation current is at least the peak input current, Iout x Vout / (Vin_min x efficiency) plus half the ripple.
The Schottky reverse voltage and output capacitor voltage are above Vout with margin, and ceramic capacitance is checked after DC-bias derating.

A plain boost has a DC path from input to output through the inductor and diode, so a shorted output is not current-limited: a fuse, PTC or load-disconnect part is present when the output leaves the board.
The IC's minimum input voltage and UVLO suit the battery chemistry's end-of-discharge voltage.
The feedback divider sits next to the FB pin and is kept away from the SW node.
The SW node copper area is small, and no sensitive traces run under the inductor.

types.name: Linear regulator board
types.description: A simple supply that drops a higher DC input to a fixed or adjustable lower rail through a linear regulator or LDO (7805, LM317, AMS1117, AP2112). It suits low-noise rails, small currents or small input-output differences, where heat (Vin - Vout) x I is acceptable. Found as breadboard power modules, analog and RF supply rails, and post-regulators after switchers.

sections.purpose: Accept the input supply and protect against reverse polarity and overload.

parts.value: 10 µF 25 V X5R (330 nF minimum for 78xx)

sections.purpose: Linear regulation to the target rail with datasheet-specified capacitors for stability.

parts.role: Output tantalum capacitor (1117-class parts need ESR in a defined range)
Alternative 5 V 1.5 A regulator with 330 nF in / 100 nF out

The output capacitor meets the regulator's stability spec: AMS1117 and LM1117 need about 10-22 µF with ESR in a defined window (tantalum), while modern LDOs are ceramic-stable.
Vin_min minus the reverse-protection diode drop still leaves at least the regulator's dropout voltage.
Input and output capacitors are within about 5 mm of the regulator pins.
The SOT-223 tab of 1117-class LDOs is VOUT, not GND: tab copper must not join the ground pour.
An LM317 has its 240 Ω R1 placed directly at OUT and ADJ, with protection diodes when the ADJ or output capacitors are large.
For TO-220 parts, the heatsink is isolated or the tab potential is accounted for (78xx tab = GND, LM317 tab = OUT).

types.name: Single-cell Li-ion charger
types.description: Charges one Li-ion or LiPo cell (4.2 V float) from USB 5 V using a CC/CV linear or switching charger IC. It usually includes cell protection (over-charge, over-discharge, over-current) and a charge-status LED. Found as TP4056-style charger modules and as the charging section of wearables, handheld devices and dev boards.
examples: Adafruit Feather onboard LiPo charging section

sections.name: USB power input
sections.purpose: Advertise as a USB sink and protect the input.

parts.role: CC1 and CC2 pull-downs, one per CC pin (UFP/sink)

sections.name: Charger IC

sections.name: Cell protection (bare cell)

The charger float-voltage variant matches the cell chemistry (4.20 V standard, 4.35 V only for HV cells; MCP73831-2 = 4.20 V).

types.name: Battery management system (BMS)
types.description: Monitors and protects a multi-cell series Li-ion or LiFePO4 pack (3S-16S and up). An analog front end (AFE) measures every cell voltage, pack current and temperature, balances cells and drives back-to-back charge/discharge MOSFETs. Used in e-bikes, power tools, energy storage, robots and UPS packs.

sections.purpose: Measure each cell voltage through RC filters and report over I2C/SPI.

sections.purpose: Bleed higher cells at more current than the AFE's internal balance FETs allow.

sections.name: Protection switches
sections.purpose: Back-to-back charge and discharge MOSFETs that disconnect the pack on a fault.

parts.value: Standoff above max pack voltage (e.g. 24 V for 5S)

sections.name: Current sense and temperature
sections.purpose: Measure pack current for coulomb counting and short-circuit detection, and sense cell temperature.

MOSFET VDS rating is at least 1.5-2 times the full-charge pack voltage, and SOA covers the short-circuit current for the programmed SCD delay.

The thermistor is mounted on or between the cells, not on the PCB near the FETs, unless a second one is intended for FET temperature.

Spacing between cell taps and HV nodes suits the pack voltage, especially on packs over 60 V.

types.name: Power bank
types.description: A portable battery pack combining a Li-ion charger, a synchronous boost converter to 5 V (or USB PD voltages) and USB output ports, often in one power-path SoC. Includes battery-level LEDs, a push button and cell protection. Consumer USB power banks and built-in battery modules in handheld and IoT products use this layout.
examples: Injoinic IP5328P / IP5389 USB-PD power banks

sections.purpose: Charge the cell and boost it to 5 V output through one switching inductor.

sections.name: USB ports
sections.purpose: Charging input and 5 V output ports with protection.

sections.name: Battery and protection

sections.name: User interface

Inductor saturation current is at least the peak battery current at minimum cell voltage (about 2.1 A x 5 V / (3.0 V x 0.9) ≈ 3.9 A plus ripple, so at least 4-5 A).
Battery traces, SoC power ground and the exposed pad use wide copper and multiple vias, since battery current is the largest current on the board.
Each CC pin on the USB-C input has its own 5.1 kΩ pull-down when no PD controller is used.
Bare cells have a protection IC and MOSFETs; cells with built-in protection are confirmed by the BOM.
The SoC thermal pad has a via array, and the layout keeps the inductor and SoC away from the cell holder.
USB-A and USB-C shells are tied to ground (directly or through an RC), and ESD protection sits at the connectors.

types.name: Solar MPPT charge controller
types.description: Charges a battery (lead-acid, LiFePO4 or Li-ion) from a photovoltaic panel while tracking the panel's maximum power point. It is a synchronous buck (or buck-boost) power stage controlled by a dedicated MPPT charger IC or an MCU that measures panel and battery voltage and current. Used in off-grid lighting, remote sensors, RVs and small solar home systems.
examples: ADI LT3652 / LT8490 MPPT demo boards

The MPPT set point (e.g. BQ24650 MPPSET divider at about 0.8 times Voc, i.e. Vmp) matches the panel datasheet.
Charge voltage and termination match the battery chemistry: lead-acid absorb/float with temperature compensation, LiFePO4 3.6 V/cell, Li-ion 4.2 V/cell.

The battery fuse sits at the battery terminal so a short anywhere on the board is protected.
The board behaves safely when the panel is connected without a battery (no output overvoltage).
Input and output hot loops are tight, and the power stage has thermal vias and copper for the MOSFETs.

types.name: DC-AC inverter
types.description: Converts a battery DC bus (12/24/48 V) into 120/230 VAC. A typical design boosts to a ~340-400 V DC link with a push-pull high-frequency transformer stage, then an H-bridge driven by SPWM produces a sine wave through an LC output filter. Used in car and RV inverters, off-grid solar systems and UPS units.
examples: TL494/SG3525 push-pull 12 V to 300-400 V boost boards
TI TIDM-SOLARUINV C2000 solar micro-inverter reference

sections.name: DC input
sections.purpose: Fuse and decouple the high-current battery input.

parts.role: Battery input fuse (ATO blade, at battery lead)

sections.name: Push-pull DC-DC boost to HV link
sections.purpose: Step the battery voltage up to the ~350-400 V DC link through a high-frequency transformer.

parts.value: Turns ratio about 1:30 for 12 V to 380 V

sections.name: H-bridge output stage
sections.purpose: Switch the DC link into a bipolar SPWM waveform.

sections.name: SPWM control and sensing
sections.purpose: Generate the sine-modulated PWM with dead time and regulate output voltage.

parts.role: HV feedback divider (several in series for voltage rating)

sections.name: Output filter and protection
sections.purpose: Filter SPWM into a clean sine wave and protect the AC output.

checks: Dead time between high- and low-side gates in each leg (typically 0.5-1.5 µs) prevents shoot-through and has been checked on a scope.
Creepage and clearance separate the low-voltage battery and control domain from the ~400 V DC link and AC output; HV feedback uses series resistors or isolation.
Bootstrap capacitors are big enough for the lowest SPWM duty and longest on-time, and bootstrap diodes are ultrafast and rated above the DC-link voltage.
H-bridge switch VDS/VCE rating has margin above the DC-link voltage (500 V parts are marginal on a 400 V link; 600 V+ parts are preferred).
Gate-drive loops are short (driver next to the FETs), with each gate resistor at its FET.
DC-link and input capacitors are rated for RMS ripple current (at 100/120 Hz and switching frequency), not just capacitance.

Battery-side current paths (100+ A on a 12 V 1 kW unit) use bus bars, thick copper or wire, and the fuse is at the battery end; low-battery cutoff, over-temperature (heatsink NTC) and output over-current shutdown are implemented.
Output neutral and earth bonding meets the target standard, and the board marks hazardous-voltage zones on silkscreen.

types.name: PoE powered-device (PD) board
types.description: Takes 37-57 V power from an Ethernet cable (IEEE 802.3af/at/bt) and converts it to isolated low-voltage rails for the device. It contains the RJ45 magnetics with centre taps, diode bridges, a PD interface (detection/classification/hot-swap) usually combined with a flyback or forward DC-DC controller, and isolated feedback. Used in IP cameras, wireless access points, VoIP phones and PoE IoT sensors.
examples: Silicon Labs Si3402 PD reference designs
ADI LTC4267 PD + regulator demo boards

checks: The detection resistor is 24.9 kΩ ±1% and sits after the bridges (on the PD side), and capacitance ahead of the hot-swap switch stays within 0.05-0.12 µF.
The classification resistor matches the class the device's power budget needs, using the controller's class table.
An SMAJ58A (or equivalent) TVS sits directly across the PD input after the bridges, close to the controller VDD/VSS pins.
The isolation between the cable, PHY-side and output domains meets 1500 Vrms (IEEE 802.3), with matching creepage and no copper crossing the barrier.
Both Mode A (data-pair centre taps) and Mode B (spare pairs) are rectified for 802.3-compliant PDs, and the bridge current rating covers the PD class (af vs at).
Flyback primary and secondary hot loops are small, and the transformer leakage clamp (RCD or Zener) keeps the primary MOSFET below its VDS rating at 57 V input.
The MagJack is specified for PoE current on its centre taps (not a data-only part with centre taps tied to 75 Ω).
Thermal relief and copper around the hot-swap FET, primary MOSFET and controller exposed pad are adequate at maximum class power.

types.name: Constant-current LED driver
types.description: Regulates the current (typically 350 mA-3 A) through a string of high-power LEDs rather than the voltage. It is usually a hysteretic or peak-current buck around a dedicated driver IC, a sense resistor, an inductor and a Schottky diode, with PWM or analog dimming. Used in LED lamps, flashlights, horticulture lights, automotive and architectural lighting.
examples: Diodes AL8860 / AL8805 LED driver EVMs
PT4115 MR16/12 V LED driver modules
Microchip HV9910B offline LED driver boards

sections.name: Input
sections.purpose: Decouple and protect the DC input.

parts.role: Input ceramic capacitor, close to VIN
Input TVS (clamp below driver abs max, e.g. 40 V)

sections.name: Driver and power stage
sections.purpose: Hysteretic buck that holds LED current constant.

parts.role: LED current sense resistor (AL8860: I = 0.1 V / Rs)

sections.name: Dimming and control
sections.purpose: PWM or analog dimming input with defined default state.

parts.role: CTRL pin filter capacitor (analog dimming / soft start)

sections.name: LED output and thermal
sections.purpose: Connect the LED string and fold back current when hot.

parts.value: JST PH 2-pin (up to about 2 A; use screw terminals above that)

checks: The sense resistor is next to the driver's sense pins, Kelvin-routed, and rated for I² x R with margin (1 A x 0.1 Ω = 0.1 W, so a 1206 at 0.25 W or more).
Minimum input voltage exceeds the LED string forward voltage at maximum current plus driver headroom (about 1-2 V for hysteretic bucks).
The inductor value and saturation current follow the datasheet so switching frequency stays within limits across the input range.
The Schottky reverse voltage exceeds Vin_max, and the input TVS clamp stays below the driver's abs-max VIN.
PWM dimming frequency and minimum pulse width suit the driver (e.g. 100 Hz-1 kHz for flicker-free hysteretic dimming).
The LEDs are on a heatsink or MCPCB with thermal foldback or a temperature limit, and the open-LED and shorted-LED behaviour is understood.
The input capacitor sits close to the driver and diode, so the hot loop is small.

types.name: Qi wireless charger (transmitter)
types.description: A WPC Qi inductive-charging transmitter that drives a resonant LC tank (transmit coil plus C0G resonant capacitors) with a full or half bridge at about 100-205 kHz. It talks to the receiver through backscatter (ASK) demodulation and runs foreign-object detection. Used in charging pads, car mounts, furniture and phone stands, typically powered from USB-C or a 12 V adapter.
examples: TI BQ500212A 5 V Qi A11 transmitter EVM
ST STWBC86 Qi transmitter evaluation kit
NXP NXQ1TXH5 single-chip 5 V Qi transmitter

sections.purpose: Bring in 5 V (or 9/12 V for higher-power profiles) and protect it.

sections.name: Transmitter controller
sections.purpose: WPC protocol, ASK demodulation, PWM generation, FOD and status.

sections.name: Bridge power stage
sections.purpose: Drive the resonant tank with a full bridge (A11) or half bridge.

parts.role: Synchronous half-bridge power block (two for a full bridge)
Half-bridge MOSFET driver (when the controller has no integrated gate drive)
Input current-sense shunt (power and FOD measurement)

sections.name: Resonant tank and coil
sections.purpose: Generate the alternating magnetic field coupled into the receiver.

parts.role: Qi A11 transmit coil with ferrite shield
Resonant capacitors (C0G, paralleled to ~400 nF for A11)
parts.value: 100 nF 50 V C0G 5 % (higher voltage for higher-power designs)

checks: The resonant capacitors are C0G/NP0 (or film), never X7R, and their voltage rating covers the measured peak tank voltage with margin (50 V C0G is typical for 5 V A11; higher-power designs can need 100 V or more).
The coil inductance and total resonant capacitance match the WPC transmitter type (A11: 6.3 µH with about 400 nF, resonance near 100 kHz).
No copper pours, ground planes or metal sit inside the coil's magnetic footprint apart from the ferrite shield, to avoid eddy losses and false FOD trips.
The bridge hot loop (input capacitors, bridge FETs, returns) is tight, and the coil leads go straight to the bridge outputs and resonant capacitors.
The input supply and connector are rated for full transmit power (5 V 2 A for 5 W A11; higher-power profiles need 9-12 V input).
An NTC near the coil and an over-temperature shutdown are present, and FOD calibration (power-loss accounting) is done with the final mechanical stack-up.
The ASK demodulation sense path follows the datasheet layout and is kept away from the bridge switching nodes.
Products sold as Qi-compatible need WPC certification and must use the certified coil and capacitor combination unchanged.

types.name: Brushed DC motor driver (H-bridge)
types.description: Drives one or two brushed DC motors in both directions with a full H-bridge. The bridge is either an integrated driver IC or four discrete MOSFETs with a gate driver, controlled by PWM and direction signals from a microcontroller. Used in robots, toys, linear actuators, pumps, door locks and small vehicles.
examples: Adafruit DRV8871 DC Motor Driver Breakout

sections.name: Driver IC and logic
sections.purpose: The integrated H-bridge, plus decoupling and defined input states so the motor stays off while the MCU boots.

parts.role: Logic supply decoupling (only for drivers with a separate VCC/VDD pin, e.g. TB6612FNG; DRV8871 has only VM)
Input pull-down (only if the driver has no internal pull-downs; DRV8871 has them)

sections.name: Motor supply (VM) decoupling
sections.purpose: Keeps VM stable against PWM ripple, motor inrush and regenerative current.

parts.role: Local VM ceramic at each VM pin

sections.name: Current limit and sensing
sections.purpose: Sets the chopping or trip current and measures motor current for stall detection.

parts.role: Current-limit set resistor (DRV8871 ILIM: I_TRIP ≈ 64 / R in kΩ; R ≥ 15 kΩ)
Low-side current shunt (discrete bridges; check P = I²R against rating)

sections.name: Input protection
sections.purpose: Protects the bridge from reverse battery connection, overvoltage spikes and short circuits.

parts.role: Reverse-polarity P-MOSFET (size for stall current; add a gate Zener and resistor when VM exceeds the ±25 V VGS rating)
TVS on VM (standoff above max supply, clamp below driver abs-max)

sections.name: Connectors and indicators

checks: VM has at least 10 µF of ceramic capacitance plus a 47-100 µF bulk electrolytic close to the driver, all rated well above the maximum supply voltage.
Every driver VM pin has its own 100 nF ceramic within a few mm, returned directly to the power ground pour.
The current-limit resistor or shunt trips above the motor's start-up current but below the driver and connector ratings.
The exposed thermal pad is soldered to a copper pour with an array of thermal vias, and the copper area is sized for the expected dissipation.
VM, OUT1/OUT2 and GND traces are sized for motor stall current, and logic ground joins power ground at one point near the driver.
The motor input has reverse-polarity protection, a TVS rated above the maximum supply, and a fuse or PTC.
Control inputs have a defined low state at reset (internal or external pull-downs), so the motor cannot spin while the MCU boots.

Motor recirculation and braking current has a path: the integrated bridge's body diodes, or Schottky freewheel diodes across discrete MOSFETs, return it to VM, and bulk capacitance or the TVS absorbs the voltage pumped up when the supply cannot sink current.

types.name: Stepper motor driver
types.description: Drives a two-phase bipolar stepper motor with chopper current regulation and microstepping, controlled by STEP/DIR signals or SPI/UART. Built as plug-in driver modules (Pololu footprint) and directly onto CNC, 3D printer, camera slider and lab automation boards.
examples: Pololu A4988 Stepper Motor Driver Carrier
Pololu DRV8825 Stepper Motor Driver Carrier

checks: Each driver has 47-100 µF bulk plus 100 nF ceramic on VS close to its power pins, rated at least 1.5x the motor supply voltage.
Sense resistors are Kelvin-routed to the driver's sense pins, rated for I²R at full current, and sized so the full-scale current matches the motor's rated phase current.
Charge-pump and internal regulator capacitors match the driver datasheet values and sit directly at their pins.
The thermal pad or ground pins connect to large copper pours with thermal vias; modules have a heatsink path for currents above about 1 A RMS.
Microstep and enable pins have defined default states, and EN defaults to disabled so motors do not energise at power-up.
The motor connector pinout (coil A pair, coil B pair) is labelled, and the board warns against hot-plugging motors while powered.
In UART/SPI mode, driver addresses (MS1/MS2 on TMC2209) are unique on a shared bus and the 1 kΩ TX series resistor is present.
The maximum motor supply, including TVS clamp and regenerative spikes, stays below the driver's VS absolute maximum (29 V for TMC2209, 35 V for A4988, 45 V for DRV8825).

types.name: BLDC electronic speed controller (ESC)
types.description: Drives a three-phase brushless DC motor from a battery through six MOSFETs in three half-bridges. A gate driver and an MCU run sensorless back-EMF or FOC commutation from PWM, DShot or CAN commands. Used in drones, RC vehicles, e-bikes, electric skateboards, fans and pumps.

sections.purpose: Runs commutation firmware (BLHeli_S/32, AM32, VESC) and reads current and voltage feedback.

parts.role: 3.3 V LDO from battery (30 V input; not needed when the gate driver has an integrated buck, e.g. DRV8323R)

sections.name: Gate driver
sections.purpose: Level-shifts MCU PWM into high-side and low-side gate drive (via charge pump or bootstrap) with dead time.

parts.role: Three-phase gate driver with current-sense amplifiers (charge-pump high-side supply)
Charge-pump flying capacitor (DRV8323 CPH-CPL, rated ≥ VM)
Bootstrap capacitor (bootstrap-type drivers such as FD6288 or IR2101 only; value per datasheet)
Gate series resistor (0 Ω with DRV8323 IDRIVE control)

sections.name: Power stage
sections.purpose: Six N-channel MOSFETs and the DC-link capacitance that supplies switching current; MOSFET body diodes carry freewheel current during dead time.

parts.role: DC-link bulk electrolytic near the battery entry

sections.name: Current and voltage sensing
sections.purpose: Shunt current measurement plus phase and battery voltage dividers for back-EMF zero-cross detection and telemetry.

parts.role: Current shunt, Kelvin-connected (small ESCs; 30 A+ designs use 0.25-1 mΩ, check P = I²R)
Phase/battery divider, bottom resistor (2.3 V at 25.2 V, below VDDA)

sections.purpose: Battery connection, transient suppression, and a protected throttle/telemetry input.

checks: Each half-bridge has low-ESR ceramic capacitance directly across its high-side drain and low-side source, and the bulk electrolytic sits as close as possible to the battery entry.
MOSFET VDS rating is at least 1.5x the maximum battery voltage (e.g. 40 V or more for 6S at 25.2 V) to cover switching and regenerative spikes.
Charge-pump or bootstrap capacitors match the gate-driver datasheet values and voltage ratings and sit right at their pins.
Gate-drive loops (driver output, gate resistor, gate, source return) are short, and all three phases are laid out symmetrically.
Shunt sense lines are Kelvin-connected to the shunt pads and routed as a differential pair to the current-sense amplifier.
Back-EMF and battery dividers keep the ADC input below VDDA at the maximum battery voltage.
Battery and phase copper is sized for continuous current (heavy copper or parallel layers), and MOSFETs have thermal vias or a heatsink path.
Dead time is set in the driver or firmware, and shoot-through and overcurrent protection are enabled.

types.name: Servo controller
types.description: Generates 50 Hz PWM pulses for multiple hobby RC servos, commanded over I2C, USB or serial, and distributes a separate high-current servo power rail. Used in robot arms, hexapods, animatronics and pan-tilt rigs.
examples: Pololu Mini Maestro 12-Channel USB Servo Controller
SparkFun Servo pHAT for Raspberry Pi

sections.purpose: A 16-channel PWM IC with decoupling, address selection and output-enable default.

parts.role: Address pin pull-down (with solder jumpers to VDD)

sections.name: I2C interface
sections.purpose: Host bus connection with pull-ups and chaining connectors.

parts.role: Host header (GND, OE, SCL, SDA, VCC, V+)

sections.name: Servo outputs
sections.purpose: Standard 3-pin servo connectors with current-limited signal lines.

At least 470 µF of bulk capacitance (about 100 µF per servo) sits on V+ near the servo headers.
V+ and GND copper is sized for the summed stall current of all servos (1-2 A each for standard servos, more for large ones).
Every PWM output has a series resistor (about 220 Ω) to limit current into a shorted or reversed servo plug.
Header pinout is GND, V+, signal with V+ in the middle, and the GND side is marked so a reversed plug is not destructive.
I2C pull-ups (4.7 kΩ) appear only once per bus, and address jumpers allow unique addresses when boards are chained.
Reverse-polarity protection, if fitted, is rated for the full servo current with acceptable voltage drop.

types.name: Relay module board
types.description: Switches mains or DC loads from a low-voltage logic signal using electromechanical relays. Each relay is driven by a transistor, often behind an optocoupler, with a flyback diode and status LED. Used in home automation, Arduino and Raspberry Pi projects, industrial I/O and lighting control.
examples: Generic 4-channel 5 V optocoupled relay module (Songle SRD-05VDC-SL-C)

sections.name: Input interface
sections.purpose: Optional optical isolation and input indication between the logic signal and the relay driver.

parts.role: Input indicator LED (often in series with the opto LED)

sections.name: Relay driver
sections.purpose: Switches the coil current and clamps the coil's inductive kickback.

parts.role: Coil driver NPN transistor (Ic ≥ 1.5x coil current)
Darlington array with built-in clamp diodes (COM to coil supply; replaces discrete drivers, up to 7 relays)

checks: Every relay coil has a flyback diode connected directly across it, cathode to the coil supply (or a ULN200x with COM tied to the coil supply).
The driver transistor's current rating is at least 1.5x the coil current, and the base resistor saturates it from the lowest supported logic level (3.3 V hosts).

Creepage and clearance between mains copper and the low-voltage side suit the working voltage (commonly 6 mm or more for reinforced isolation at 250 VAC), with routed slots under the relay where needed.
Contact traces are sized for the relay's rated current using an IPC-2152 calculator, or widened, exposed and tinned.
Inputs default to relay-off at power-up and during MCU reset (base or input pull-down).
If isolation is claimed, the JD-VCC and logic grounds really are separate and the optocoupler bridges the gap.
Terminal block voltage and current ratings meet or exceed the relay contact rating, and the silkscreen states the relay's real AC rating (e.g. 8 A at 250 VAC for G5LE).

types.name: Drone flight controller
types.description: Stabilises and navigates a multirotor or fixed-wing aircraft. A fast MCU fuses IMU, barometer and GPS data and outputs DShot or PWM commands to the ESCs. Common in 30.5 mm and 20 mm FPV stacks running Betaflight or INAV, and in larger ArduPilot/PX4 autopilots.

parts.role: BOOT0 pull-down (with DFU button or pad)
3.3 V LDO (fed from the 5 V BEC)

sections.name: Clock and USB

parts.role: Crystal load capacitor (size to crystal CL)

sections.name: Sensors
sections.purpose: Gyro/accelerometer and barometer with a clean, filtered supply.

sections.name: 5 V BEC and battery input

The IMU sits near the board centre, away from the buck inductor and switch node, on a filtered supply (ferrite or RC), with its interrupt line routed to the MCU.
The battery input has a TVS and input capacitors rated for the maximum cell count (6S = 25.2 V, so 50 V ceramics), placed at the buck input.
The buck has its inductor, input and output ceramics and bootstrap capacitor placed tightly per the datasheet layout, with a small switch-node area.
The VBAT divider keeps the ADC below 3.3 V at maximum battery voltage, and the scale factor is documented for firmware.
USB-C has 5.1 kΩ pull-downs on each CC pin individually and ESD protection on D+/D-.
The barometer is kept away from LEDs and airflow (foam cover), and the gyro uses a dedicated SPI bus.
Mounting holes match the 30.5x30.5 mm (M3) or 20x20 mm (M2) stack standard, and the ESC connector pinout matches common 4in1 ESCs.

types.name: 3D printer mainboard

It drives 4-8 stepper axes, switches the hotend and bed heaters and fans through MOSFETs, and reads thermistors, endstops and probes. Typically powered from 12 V or 24 V, with USB and microSD for host connection and job storage.

sections.purpose: The motion-control MCU with decoupling, core capacitors, crystal and its 3.3 V LDO.

parts.role: 3.3 V LDO (fed from the 5 V buck)

sections.name: Stepper driver channels
sections.purpose: One driver per axis or extruder, each with its own motor supply decoupling and current sensing.

sections.name: Heater and fan outputs
