checks: Heater MOSFET gates have a pull-down so heaters stay off while the MCU is in reset or the bootloader, and BOOT0 is pulled down so the board boots from flash.
Heated-bed current path (terminal, traces, MOSFET, fuse) is rated for bed current (often 10-15 A at 24 V), with a separate fuse from the motor and logic rail.
Each stepper driver has its own bulk and ceramic capacitance on VM, and thermal pads have vias to inner or bottom copper.
Thermistor pull-ups are 4.7 kΩ to the ADC reference (not a noisy rail), with filter capacitors next to the MCU pin.
All supply-rated parts (capacitors, TVS, MOSFETs) are rated for 24 V operation with margin, even when the board is sold for 12 V.
Fan and other inductive outputs have flyback diodes, and 5 V/24 V fan voltage selection is clearly marked.
USB-C has 5.1 kΩ CC pull-downs and ESD protection, and USB VBUS cannot back-feed the 5 V rail when 24 V is off (diode or switch).
The 5 V buck has its inductor, input and output ceramics placed tightly per the datasheet layout, and microSD CMD/DAT lines have 10 kΩ pull-ups.

types.name: Robot controller
types.description: The central control board of a mobile robot or manipulator. It combines an MCU (or an SBC interface), several motor drivers, encoder and sensor inputs, servo outputs, an IMU, and buses such as CAN, UART and USB, all powered from a battery. Used in educational and competition robots, AGVs and ROS platforms.

sections.name: MCU and clock
sections.purpose: The real-time controller that runs motor loops, reads encoders and talks to the host.

parts.role: VDD decoupling (also one at each transceiver/sensor supply pin)

sections.name: Battery input protection
sections.purpose: Fusing, reverse-polarity and transient protection and bulk storage at the battery entry.

parts.role: Reverse-polarity P-MOSFET (VGS ±25 V covers up to 5S)

sections.name: Logic regulation
sections.purpose: A 5 V buck from the battery and a 3.3 V LDO for the MCU and sensors.

parts.role: 5 V buck regulator (adjustable, FB divider sets 5 V)

sections.name: Motor drivers
sections.purpose: H-bridges for drive and actuator motors, with supply decoupling and current limits.

parts.role: VM bulk ceramic (plus the shared input electrolytic)

sections.name: Sensor and encoder I/O
sections.purpose: Quadrature encoder inputs, IMU, I2C sensor bus and ESD protection on external lines.

sections.name: Communication
sections.purpose: CAN for smart actuators and USB for a host computer or ROS.

parts.role: CAN transceiver (VIO pin for 3.3 V logic)

checks: The battery input has a fuse, reverse-polarity protection and a TVS rated above the maximum pack voltage.
Motor-driver ground returns and VM currents do not flow through the MCU, IMU or encoder ground paths; power and signal grounds join at one point.
Every motor driver has local 100 nF plus bulk capacitance on VM, and current limits are set below connector and trace ratings.
The 5 V buck has its inductor and input/output ceramics placed tightly per the datasheet, and the 3.3 V LDO has its input and output capacitors.
Encoder inputs connect to MCU timer pins that support quadrature mode, with pull-ups and RC filtering where cables are long.
Servo headers (if present) are powered from a separate 5-6 V rail sized for stall current, not from the logic 5 V.
Every connector that leaves the board has ESD protection, and CAN termination is jumper-selectable at the 120 Ω bus ends.
The IMU is mounted rigidly near the robot's rotation centre, away from motors and the buck inductor, and its axis orientation is marked in silkscreen.

types.name: Isolated gate driver board
types.description: Drives the gates of high-voltage IGBTs or SiC/GaN MOSFETs across a galvanic isolation barrier. It includes an isolated bipolar bias supply, gate resistors, desaturation (short-circuit) protection and fault feedback to the controller. Used in motor inverters, EV traction and chargers, solar inverters, UPS systems and industrial drives.
examples: Wolfspeed CGD15HB62P1 SiC MOSFET gate driver

sections.name: Primary (logic) side
sections.purpose: The isolated driver's input side, with decoupling, input noise filtering and fault reporting.

parts.role: Isolated single-channel gate driver with DESAT and Miller clamp

sections.name: Isolated bias supply
sections.purpose: A floating bipolar supply (e.g. +15 V / -5 V) for each secondary, decoupled for peak gate current.

parts.role: Transformer driver (alternative to a DC/DC module)

sections.name: Gate output network
sections.purpose: Sets turn-on and turn-off speed and keeps the gate safely off and clamped.

parts.role: Turn-on gate resistor (check pulse rating; anti-surge types preferred)
Gate clamp Zener (back-to-back pair so negative bias is not clamped)

sections.name: Desaturation protection
sections.purpose: Detects short circuits by sensing collector/drain voltage after a blanking time, then turns off softly.

parts.role: DESAT high-voltage blocking diode (VR ≥ DC bus voltage; series for higher buses)
DESAT blanking capacitor (t ≈ C·V_DESAT / I_CHG; 220 pF ≈ 4 µs on ISO5852S, use ~100 pF for SiC)

sections.name: Connectors and indicators
sections.purpose: Controller interface, connection to the power module, and fault indication.

parts.role: Controller interface header (PWM, FLT, RDY, supply)

checks: Creepage and clearance across the isolation barrier, and between high-side and low-side secondaries, meet the system isolation standard (e.g. IEC 60664-1 / 61800-5-1) for the DC bus voltage; no copper, vias or pours bridge the gap under the driver or DC/DC.
The gate loop (driver output, gate resistor, gate, Kelvin emitter/source, VEE2) is short with minimal loop area and uses the module's auxiliary emitter or Kelvin-source pin.
VCC2 and VEE2 each have 100 nF plus at least 1 µF ceramic at the driver pins, and enough bulk capacitance to deliver peak gate charge without significant droop.
Gate resistors are pulse-rated for the peak gate current, and their average dissipation (about Qg × ΔVgate × fsw) is within rating.
A 10 kΩ gate-emitter pull-down and a bidirectional clamp keep the switch off and protected when the driver is unpowered.
The DESAT diode reverse rating exceeds the DC bus voltage, and the blanking time is shorter than the switch's short-circuit withstand time (about 10 µs for IGBTs, 2-3 µs for SiC).
Driver CMTI (100 kV/µs or more for SiC) and the isolation rating of both driver and DC/DC suit the application's dV/dt and working voltage.
FLT/RDY outputs are pulled up on the primary side and wired so a fault blocks PWM at the controller.

types.name: Class-D Audio Amplifier
types.description: A switching (class-D) power amplifier board that drives passive speakers from line-level or I2S input, typically 2x10 W to 2x100 W from a 12-24 V supply. Used in powered speakers, soundbars, Bluetooth speakers and DIY amp modules.

sections.name: Amplifier IC and supply decoupling
sections.purpose: The class-D power stage draws large pulsed currents; each PVCC pin needs a local high-frequency cap plus a shared bulk electrolytic to keep the rail stiff and limit EMI. The internal gate-drive (GVDD) and analog (AVCC) supplies need their own datasheet capacitors.

parts.package: HTSSOP-32 PowerPAD (DAD = pad up, needs heatsink)

sections.name: Input stage
sections.purpose: AC-couples the line input into the amplifier and sets gain; for I2S parts this is the digital interface instead.

parts.qty: 1 per input pin (4 for stereo differential)

sections.name: Output LC filter
sections.purpose: Removes the PWM carrier from the speaker leads to meet EMI limits and protect tweeters; corner frequency typically 30-40 kHz (TPA3116 reference: 10 uH + 680 nF for 4-8 ohm).

parts.value: 10 uH, Isat above peak speaker current

sections.name: Power input and protection
sections.purpose: Accepts the DC supply, protects against reverse polarity and overvoltage, and fuses the rail.

parts.role: Reverse polarity Schottky (or P-MOSFET for lower loss)

parts.value: 24 V standoff, 600 W (choose so clamp stays below the IC absolute max)
sized for ~2 mA (e.g. 10 kΩ at 24 V)

sections.name: Control and fault
sections.purpose: Mute/shutdown sequencing and open-drain fault reporting to avoid pops and report over-current or thermal shutdown.

parts.role: SDZ power-up delay capacitor (RC with the pull-up)

checks: Every PVCC pin has a 100 nF to 1 uF X7R capacitor within about 2 mm, returned straight to the power ground
The PowerPAD is handled for its orientation: a pad-down part (e.g. TPA3118D2 DAP) is soldered to a copper pour with a via array, a pad-up part (TPA3116D2 DAD) has a heatsink fitted
Output inductors are rated for saturation current above the peak speaker current, and the LC corner sits at about 30-40 kHz for the speaker impedance
In a BTL design neither speaker terminal goes to ground, and the speaker connectors are not shared with chassis ground
Bulk electrolytic voltage rating is at least 1.25x the maximum PVCC, and the TVS clamp voltage stays below the amplifier's absolute-maximum PVCC
Analog input ground and power ground are separated and join at a single point near the IC GND pins
Gain and mode resistor values match the datasheet table for the intended gain and master/slave or PBTL mode
Bootstrap capacitors sit at the BSxx pins, GVDD/AVCC caps are at their pins, and the switching node loops (OUT-L-C) are as small as possible

types.name: USB Audio DAC / Headphone Amplifier
types.description: A bus-powered USB sound card that enumerates as a USB Audio Class device, converts to analog, and drives headphones or line out. Found in USB-C dongles, desktop DAC/amps and USB headsets.

sections.name: USB interface and protection
sections.purpose: Brings in VBUS and data, identifies the board as a sink and protects data lines from ESD.

parts.role: D+/D- series resistors (only if the codec datasheet shows them)

sections.name: USB audio codec and clock
sections.purpose: The USB-to-audio bridge or DAC IC needs a clean crystal reference and per-pin decoupling.

parts.value: 2 x (CL - Cstray): about 12-15 pF C0G for a 10 pF crystal (18-22 pF for an 18 pF crystal)

sections.name: Analog supply
sections.purpose: A low-noise LDO isolates the DAC and headphone amp from noisy USB VBUS.

sections.name: Headphone output stage
sections.purpose: Buffers the DAC output into 16-300 Ω headphones; ground-referenced (DirectPath) amps need no output coupling caps.

checks: CC1 and CC2 each have their own 5.1 kΩ pull-down to GND; a single shared resistor is not a valid sink termination
The ESD array sits next to the USB connector, D+/D- are routed as a 90 Ω differential pair, and there are no stubs
Series resistors on D+/D- are fitted only when the codec datasheet calls for them
Crystal load capacitors match the crystal's CL (C = 2 x (CL - Cstray)) and sit within a few mm of the oscillator pins
Analog and digital supplies are separated by a ferrite or LDO, and the analog ground return does not carry USB digital current
If the headphone amp is not ground-referenced, output DC-blocking capacitors (100-220 uF) are present
Total VBUS capacitance at attach stays within the USB limit of 10 uF

types.name: Microphone Preamplifier
types.description: A low-noise balanced-input amplifier that raises microphone-level signals (-60 to -20 dBu) to line level, often with switchable +48 V phantom power for condenser mics. Used in audio interfaces, mixers, field recorders and standalone preamp modules.
examples: TI INA217 microphone preamp reference design

sections.name: Balanced input and RF filtering
sections.purpose: Accepts the balanced mic signal, blocks phantom DC from the amp and filters RF before the first gain stage.

parts.role: Input bias resistors to ground (after the DC block)

sections.name: Phantom power
sections.purpose: Feeds +48 V through matched resistors to both legs of the XLR for condenser microphones, per IEC 61938, switched per channel.

parts.value: 6.81 kΩ 0.1%, ≥0.25 W (a shorted input dissipates about 0.34 W)
-60 V P-channel MOSFET (front-panel switch drives the gate)

sections.name: Gain stage and input protection
sections.purpose: Low-noise instrumentation amp provides 0-60 dB of gain; clamp diodes protect it from phantom hot-plug transients.

sections.name: Output buffer and supply
sections.purpose: Drives line-level output or the ADC and supplies clean bipolar rails.

checks: The two phantom feed resistors are matched to 0.1% or better, rated for the shorted-input dissipation, and both legs of the XLR see identical networks for CMRR
DC-blocking capacitors are rated at least 63 V and oriented with + toward the XLR, since phantom puts +48 V there
Clamp diodes plus series resistors protect the amp inputs from the hot-plug transient when phantom is switched or a mic is connected
RF filter capacitors are C0G, placed at the connector, and the differential capacitor is larger than the common-mode capacitors
The XLR pin 1 shield bonds to chassis at the connector, not to the signal ground, to avoid the pin-1 problem
The gain resistor and its traces are short and symmetric, and the input traces run as a tight differential pair away from digital lines
Every op-amp and in-amp supply pin has a 100 nF cap at the pin, plus local bulk capacitance

types.name: LED Matrix / Addressable LED Board
types.description: A board carrying arrays of addressable RGB LEDs (WS2812B, SK6812, APA102) or a multiplexed LED matrix driven by a controller such as the MAX7219 or IS31FL3731. Used in signage, light panels, wearables, keyboards and decorative lighting.

sections.name: Addressable LED array
sections.purpose: Each smart LED needs its own decoupling capacitor; the data line daisy-chains from DOUT to DIN.

parts.value: 5 V, about 60 mA max at full white

parts.role: Data-line series resistor at first LED

sections.name: Controller and logic-level shifting
sections.purpose: A 3.3 V MCU cannot reliably drive a 5 V WS2812 data input; a 5 V-supplied AHCT buffer shifts the level.

parts.role: 3.3 V to 5 V level shifter buffer

parts.value: 100 nF X7R 16 V (plus 10 uF bulk at the module)
per datasheet table (≥9.53 kΩ, about 10 kΩ for ~40 mA segment)

sections.name: Power distribution
sections.purpose: LED arrays draw amps at 5 V; bulk capacitance at the injection point prevents inrush damage and rail droop.

checks: Every addressable LED has a 100 nF capacitor next to its VDD pin
The data input to the first LED is level-shifted to 5 V logic (VIH about 0.7 x VDD) when the controller runs at 3.3 V
A series resistor of about 330 Ω sits close to the first LED's DIN to damp reflections
The power budget (about 60 mA per WS2812B at full white) matches trace widths, connector rating and fuse, with power injected every 50-100 LEDs on long chains
A bulk capacitor of at least 470 uF sits at each power entry point, and the controller's ground is common with the LED supply ground
DOUT-to-DIN chain order matches the pixel mapping the firmware expects (serpentine or progressive)
Thermal: copper pours spread heat in dense arrays, and brightness is limited in firmware if the supply cannot support full white

types.name: Mechanical Keyboard PCB
types.description: A key-matrix PCB with MX or Choc switch footprints (often hot-swap sockets), one diode per key, a USB MCU running QMK/ZMK/VIA firmware, and optional per-key RGB. Used in custom and commercial mechanical keyboards and macropads.
examples: Raspberry Pi RP2040 keyboard designs (e.g. Ferris/Sweep)

sections.name: Key matrix
sections.purpose: Switches are wired in a row/column matrix with one diode per key to prevent ghosting and allow full N-key rollover.

sections.name: MCU and clock
sections.purpose: The USB-capable MCU scans the matrix; ATmega32U4 needs a 16 MHz crystal, and RP2040 needs a 12 MHz crystal (with a 1 kΩ series resistor) plus external QSPI flash.

sections.name: USB interface and protection
sections.purpose: USB-C sink with CC pull-downs, ESD protection, MCU-recommended series resistors and a VBUS polyfuse.

sections.name: Power, buttons and RGB
sections.purpose: A 3.3 V LDO for RP2040-class MCUs, reset/boot buttons for flashing, plus optional per-key or underglow addressable LEDs.

checks: Every key has exactly one diode, and all diodes face the same direction to match the firmware DIODE_DIRECTION (COL2ROW or ROW2COL)
Switch and hot-swap footprints match the chosen switch family (MX vs Choc) and the plate cut-out grid of 19.05 mm (MX)
CC1 and CC2 each have their own 5.1 kΩ pull-down, and D+/D- run as a 90 Ω pair with ESD protection at the connector
USB series resistors match the MCU datasheet: 27 Ω for RP2040, 22 Ω for ATmega32U4
The crystal and load caps sit next to the MCU, and the RP2040 QSPI flash traces are short and kept off the key matrix
An accessible reset/boot button or pads exist for flashing (BOOTSEL on RP2040, RESET on 32U4)
The RGB current budget stays below 500 mA from USB, with brightness capped in firmware if needed

types.name: Game Controller
types.description: A handheld input device with analog sticks, triggers, buttons, a wireless or USB MCU, a Li-ion battery and charger, and often rumble motors and an IMU. Used in console and PC gamepads, arcade sticks and mobile controllers.

sections.name: Inputs
sections.purpose: Analog sticks feed ADC pins; buttons need debouncing and pull-ups (internal or external).

sections.name: Wireless MCU
sections.purpose: A BLE or Wi-Fi SoC runs the HID stack; a certified module avoids RF layout and approval work.

sections.name: Battery charging and protection
sections.purpose: Single-cell Li-ion charging from USB with input/output capacitors, a programmed charge current, cell temperature sensing and protection.

parts.role: Battery NTC thermistor (with a TS/THERM-capable charger such as MCP73833, or in the pack)

sections.name: Regulation and fuel gauge
sections.purpose: Load-sharing power path so the system runs while charging, a 3.3 V regulator and an optional fuel gauge.

sections.name: Rumble and USB
sections.purpose: Low-side MOSFET drives ERM vibration motors with flyback diodes; USB-C provides charging and wired mode.

checks: Each vibration motor has a flyback diode across it and its MOSFET gate has a pull-down so the motor stays off during boot
The antenna keep-out of the wireless module is respected: no copper or ground pour under or near the antenna, and the antenna sits at the board edge
Joystick wiper outputs go to ADC-capable pins with a filter cap, and the stick reference rail is the ADC reference

The charger's PROG resistor sets a charge current at or below 1C of the battery, the charger has its input and output capacitors, and the cell has protection and temperature sensing (on the pack or the board)
CC1/CC2 5.1 kΩ pull-downs and USB ESD protection are present at the connector
Button footprints line up with the enclosure button caps and the shoulder/trigger mechanisms
Every MCU and IC supply pin has a 100 nF capacitor, and the radio module has bulk capacitance for TX current peaks

types.name: Smartwatch / Wearable Board
types.description: A very small, dense, battery-powered board with a BLE SoC, display connector, IMU, heart-rate/SpO2 sensor and a wearable PMIC. Used in fitness bands, smartwatches, rings and health trackers.

sections.name: BLE SoC and clocks
sections.purpose: The radio SoC needs a 32 MHz HF crystal for BLE timing, an optional 32.768 kHz crystal for low-power sleep, and an RF matching network per the vendor reference.

parts.value: 32 MHz ±10 ppm, CL about 8 pF (per Nordic reference)

parts.role: DC/DC regulator inductor (if internal buck used)

sections.name: Power management
sections.purpose: A wearable PMIC charges a small Li-Po (40-300 mAh) and provides low-quiescent rails for long standby.

parts.role: Battery NTC thermistor (if the cell has none)

sections.name: Sensors
sections.purpose: Motion and optical heart-rate sensing on I2C/SPI with pull-ups and per-sensor decoupling.

sections.name: Display and haptics
sections.purpose: FPC connector to a small LCD/OLED/e-paper display, plus a vibration motor for notifications.

parts.value: 0.5 mm pitch FPC, pin count per panel

checks: The RF matching network and antenna follow the SoC vendor's reference layout exactly, with the ground clearance the antenna needs
The HF crystal (32 MHz on nRF52) and the LF crystal sit within a few mm of the SoC, with load caps matched to each crystal's CL
Every SoC VDD pin has its datasheet decoupling capacitor, and the DC/DC inductor values match the reference when the internal buck is used
The PMIC charge current suits the small battery (0.5-1C), and a battery NTC is fitted when the cell lacks one
I2C pull-ups go to the same rail as the sensors' VDDIO, with only one set per bus
The PPG sensor sits flush with the rear window, with no copper or silkscreen in its optical path
Board outline, keep-outs and component heights fit the enclosure; check 0201/0402 placement and via-in-pad for WLCSP/BGA parts

types.name: Smart Home Switch / Plug
types.description: A mains-powered connected device that switches an AC load with a relay or triac, often with power metering, controlled over Wi-Fi, Zigbee, Thread or BLE. Used in smart plugs, in-wall relays, dimmers and light switches.

sections.name: Mains input and protection
sections.purpose: Fuses the AC line, clamps surges and feeds a compact isolated AC-DC supply.

sections.name: Low-voltage rail and MCU
sections.purpose: Regulates 3.3 V for a Wi-Fi/BLE module and decouples its TX current bursts.

sections.name: Load switching
sections.purpose: A relay (on/off) or triac with a random-phase optocoupler driver (dimming) switches the AC load under MCU control.

sections.name: Power metering (optional)
sections.purpose: Measures load voltage and current via a shunt and a metering IC for energy monitoring.

checks: Creepage and clearance between mains and SELV meets IEC 62368-1 (typically at least 6 mm reinforced for 230 V), with a slot under optocouplers and the AC-DC module where needed
Relay contact rating and trace width/thickness handle the rated load current (for example 10 A needs wide pours or 2 oz copper, or a solder-reinforced trace)
A fuse and MOV are present on the mains input, with the fuse upstream of the MOV
The relay coil has a flyback diode and the driver transistor is sized for the coil current
Metering divider resistors are split across several parts to meet each resistor's voltage rating
The antenna keep-out of the radio module is clear of mains copper and the relay, and the antenna faces the enclosure's plastic side
The MCU ground is referenced correctly: for non-isolated metering designs the whole low-voltage side is at mains potential and must not be user-accessible

types.name: PLC Digital I/O Module
types.description: An industrial 24 V digital input/output card that reads sensors and switches (IEC 61131-2 Type 1/3 inputs) and drives solenoids, relays and lamps through protected high-side outputs, galvanically isolated from the controller logic. Used in PLC expansion modules, remote I/O and machine controllers.

sections.name: 24 V supply input and protection
sections.purpose: Field supply entry with reverse-polarity, surge and fuse protection per IEC 61131-2.

parts.role: Supply fuse (a PTC must be rated ≥33 V)

sections.name: Isolated digital inputs
sections.purpose: Reads 24 V field signals across an isolation barrier with defined current-limiting and switching thresholds.

parts.role: Input status LED (in the field current path, or logic-driven with its own resistor)

sections.name: Protected digital outputs
sections.purpose: High-side switches drive inductive loads with built-in current limit, thermal shutdown and demagnetisation clamps.

sections.name: Isolation and logic interface
sections.purpose: Digital isolators and an isolated DC-DC supply separate field side from the controller backplane.

checks: The isolation barrier has the creepage/clearance required by the module's rated working voltage, with no copper crossing it except isolator and transformer footprints
Input current-limit and threshold resistors give the IEC 61131-2 Type 1/3 ON/OFF thresholds the datasheet specifies
Every field terminal has surge protection (TVS or an IC rated for IEC 61000-4-5) and inputs survive reverse 24 V
High-side outputs are rated for the inductive load energy, or an external freewheel/TVS is fitted
Supply and output traces are sized for the total module current, the thermal pad of the output driver has a via array, and fuses/PTCs are rated for the 24-33 V supply
Status LEDs per channel are driven from the field side or from logic consistently, with correct series resistors
The terminal pinout and silkscreen legends match the datasheet / wiring diagram for each channel

types.name: Automotive ECU / CAN Node
types.description: An electronic control unit or CAN bus node powered from the 12 V vehicle battery, with load-dump and reverse-battery protection, a CAN or CAN-FD transceiver and an automotive MCU. Used in body controllers, sensor nodes, dashboards, data loggers and aftermarket modules.

sections.name: Battery input protection
sections.purpose: Survives reverse battery, ISO 7637-2 / ISO 16750-2 load-dump and cranking transients on the 12 V supply.

parts.value: 26 V standoff 600 W for suppressed load dump (SM8S class for unsuppressed)

sections.name: Regulation
sections.purpose: A wide-input, low-quiescent regulator rated for 40 V transients supplies the 5 V / 3.3 V logic.

parts.role: LDO output capacitor (ESR inside the datasheet stability window)

sections.name: MCU and clock
sections.purpose: CAN bit timing needs a crystal (not an RC oscillator) for frequency accuracy.

parts.value: 2 x (CL - Cstray): about 27 pF C0G for an 18 pF crystal

sections.name: CAN physical layer
sections.purpose: The transceiver drives CANH/CANL; split termination, a common-mode choke and ESD diodes improve EMC and robustness.

checks: The input survives reverse battery and the ISO 16750-2 load-dump profile (suppressed load dump about 35-40 V), and the regulator's max input exceeds the clamp voltage
Exactly two nodes on a bus are terminated, either 120 Ω or split 2 x 60.4 Ω with a 4.7 nF midpoint cap; mid-bus nodes have termination unpopulated
CANH/CANL are routed as a tight differential pair, with ESD diodes at the connector and the CM choke between connector and transceiver
The MCU uses a crystal for the CAN clock and the bit timing gives a sample point near 80-87.5%
Parts are AEC-Q100/Q200 qualified where the product needs them, and the temperature range covers -40 to +85/105 °C
Every IC supply pin has a 100 nF capacitor, the LDO output capacitor meets its ESR stability requirement, and the transceiver's VIO matches the MCU logic level
Connector pinout matches the harness, with a separate ground return and a wake/ignition input where needed

types.name: Data Acquisition (DAQ) Front-End
types.description: A multichannel precision measurement board with input protection, anti-alias filtering, a high-resolution delta-sigma or SAR ADC, a precision voltage reference and often galvanic isolation to the host. Used in lab DAQ, sensor loggers, strain-gauge/thermocouple readers and industrial analog input cards.

sections.name: Input protection and anti-alias filtering
sections.purpose: Protects ADC inputs from overvoltage and ESD and band-limits the signal before sampling.

parts.value: dual series small-signal diode (low-leakage type for high-impedance inputs)
1 nF C0G 50 V (about 1/10 of the differential cap)

sections.name: Signal conditioning
sections.purpose: Instrumentation amplifiers or ADC drivers provide gain, impedance buffering and common-mode rejection.

sections.name: ADC and reference
sections.purpose: The high-resolution converter, its clock (e.g. a 7.68 MHz crystal on the ADS1256) and its voltage reference set the accuracy; all need careful decoupling.

sections.name: Isolation and host interface
sections.purpose: Galvanic isolation breaks ground loops between the sensor side and the host PC or controller.

checks: The ADC reference has the output capacitor its datasheet requires, and the reference is placed close to the ADC REFP/REFN pins
The anti-alias filter is symmetric on both legs of each differential input, with C0G capacitors and a differential cap at least 10x the common-mode caps
Input protection keeps ADC pins within absolute-maximum ratings at the specified overvoltage, and the series resistors are rated for the fault power
Precision gain and divider resistors are 0.1% thin film with low tempco; no thick-film parts in the signal path
There is a solid analog ground plane under the ADC, with digital SPI lines and the ADC clock routed away from analog inputs and the reference
Every ADC, op-amp and reference supply pin is decoupled at the pin; the analog and digital supplies are separated by a ferrite or LDO
When isolated, creepage meets the rated working voltage and no ground or shield copper crosses the barrier

types.name: Medical ECG Front-End
types.description: A biopotential acquisition board that measures microvolt-level heart signals from skin electrodes using a dedicated ECG AFE with right-leg drive, lead-off detection and high common-mode rejection, with patient-side isolation. Used in heart-rate monitors, Holter recorders, ECG patches and medical/fitness development kits.
examples: Analog Devices AD8232 heart-rate monitor (SparkFun breakout)

sections.name: Electrode inputs and protection
sections.purpose: Limits current into the patient and into the AFE, filters RF and protects against ESD and defibrillation pulses.

parts.value: 10-50 kΩ (use pulse-withstanding parts for defibrillation-proof designs)

sections.name: ECG analog front-end
sections.purpose: The AFE provides programmable gain, high-resolution conversion, lead-off detection and right-leg drive for common-mode rejection.

parts.value: per datasheet pin (1 uF, 10 uF, 22 uF on ADS1292R VCAP/VREFP)

sections.name: Isolated power and data
sections.purpose: Separates the patient side from mains-connected hosts; battery operation is preferred for patient-connected prototypes.

parts.role: Isolation transformer (rated for the required MOPP)

sections.name: MCU and indicators
sections.purpose: A low-power MCU reads the AFE over SPI and streams data; the DRDY interrupt and lead-off status drive the indicators.

checks: Every electrode path has a series resistor that limits patient auxiliary current (IEC 60601-1, about 10 uA DC normal condition for CF parts) and protects the AFE
The patient side is isolated from any mains-connected equipment (2 MOPP for medical use) or the board runs only on a battery
The input RC filters are matched on both legs of each channel, with C0G capacitors, to preserve CMRR
The right-leg drive output connects to the RL electrode through its series resistor, and the RLD loop is stable per the datasheet's R/C values
Electrode traces are short, symmetric and guarded, kept away from the SPI clock and switching regulators
AFE reference and VCAP capacitors match the datasheet values and sit at the pins, and every supply pin is decoupled
Lead-off detection is enabled and its current (DC or AC) is set to the datasheet range for the electrode type

types.name: Prototyping / Perfboard-Style Adapter Board
types.description: A simple breakout, adapter or proto board that brings a fine-pitch IC, module or connector out to 2.54 mm headers, often with a regulator, power LED and decoupling. Used for breadboarding, SOIC/QFN-to-DIP adapters, sensor breakouts and perfboard-style proto shields.

sections.name: Headers and interconnect
sections.purpose: Brings every target pin out to 0.1-inch headers for breadboards, perfboards or jumper wires.

sections.name: Power and regulation
sections.purpose: Optional on-board regulator so the breakout runs from 5 V while the target IC runs at 3.3 V.

sections.name: Bus support

types.name: LoRa / sub-GHz radio board

Module footprint, keep-outs, thermal ground vias and USB/debug test points match the hardware integration manual
